limitations: Annotation figure fields keep caption-layer status not_inspected; the actual JPEG was inspected in the separate visual submission.
Figure 1 panel ownership unresolved: no A/B/C/D-to-patient mapping, although all four narratives cite Figure 1.

Abstract reports anastomotic strictures in all four patients and results describe a stricture/narrowing for each, but the discussion says 3 of 4 patients with strictures "one of whom required surgical revision"; no patient is identified as the revised one and no patient-specific negative stricture claim is invented.
Abstract age-at-surgery range 2-11 years conflicts with Table 1 ages at surgery 2, 10, 6, 2 (maximum 10); table/case-specific values retained.
Methods say endoscopy used a flexible endoscope under general anesthesia, but the P1 paragraph says a rigid scope; both wordings retained.

The discussion sentence on PedsQL scores contains garbled wording ("metformin-induced Cobalamin (B12) deficiency threshold of 60"); only the clear statement that three patients (aged 3, 6, 11) had psychosocial impairments and the 23-year-old had uniformly high scores is used.
P1 and P2 paragraphs cite the wrong table for some findings (P1 imaging cites Table 2; P2 endoscopy cites Table 3); text retained as written.
P4 longitudinal documentation gaps (including a phase lost to follow-up) and the unavailable referring-facility operative report for P3 limit details.

Series-level surgical technique (isoperistaltic transverse colon graft, retrosternal tunnel, three anastomoses) and "native esophagus left in situ" are not patient-specific operative notes; kept review-only except where individual imaging shows a native esophagus (P2, P3).
No explicit same-patient prior-report linkage identified; cited literature cohorts (Ahmed et al., Coopman et al., Amin et al.) are external and not patient facts.

PedsQL form per patient: methods state the Young Adult Version was used for participants above 18, which applies only to P4 (23 years); self-report versus parent-proxy forms for P1-P3 are not stated. No pre-operative PedsQL exists, so current scores do not establish change.

Series-level timing inconsistencies: patients were "identified from the hospital´s esophageal replacement surgery database over five years (2014-2019)" and abstract says "Median follow-up exceeded five years", yet P4 had replacement at age 2 and is now 23, while P1 (2 to 3 years) and P3 (6 to 6 years) have about one year or less of post-replacement follow-up. No surgery dates or follow-up durations are inferred.
